section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Femininity Ideology Scale (FIS; Lehman, 2000), a 45-item measure scored on a 5-point Likert scale, with factor scores computed as means of items and an overall Total Traditional score. It reports internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) for five subscales (.88, .85, .88, .89, .83) and for the total score (.93). There is no mention of Study 1, experiment numbering, sample size, participant demographics, BMI assessment, or correlations with body appreciation in this text.
section_summary.evidence_source: The FIS is a 45-item scale that measures the degree to which respondents endorse traditional femininity ideology along five dimensions (see above). In the present study, Cronbach's alpha for the five subscales were: Stereotypic Image and Activities, .88; Dependence/Deference, .85; Purity, .88; Caretaking, .89, and; Emotionality, .83. For the Total Traditional score, Cronbach's alpha was .93.
